questions.question: A celt is ______ from the Neolithic period.
questions.solution:
• Meaning: A Tool
  • Type: A Celt is typically a polished stone axe or adze used by Neolithic humans for woodworking or farming.

questions.question: As described in ‘Ain-i-Akbari’ by Abul Fazl-i-Allami, ‘gaz’ (unit of measuring length) was divided into equal parts called ______.
questions.solution:
• Unit: Tassuj
  • Measurement: One Gaz was equal to 24 Tassuj in the measurement system refined by Akbar.

questions.question: The Mughal court chronicles are written in ______.
questions.solution:
• Language: Persian
  • Reason: Persian was the official court language of the Mughals, replacing Turkish over time.

questions.question: Who among the following was a contributor to the subject of medicine in ancient India?
questions.solution:
• Person: Charaka
  • Work: Known as the 'Father of Indian Medicine', he authored the Charaka Samhita.

questions.question: At which of the following jails was Khudiram Bose sent to the gallows?
questions.solution:
• Jail: Muzaffarpur
  • Event: Executed at age 18 for attempting to assassinate British judge Douglas Kingsford in 1908.

questions.question: Who among the following was an ancient Indian mathematician-astronomer?
questions.solution:
• Person: Varahamihira
  • Work: Author of Pancha-Siddhantika and Brihat Samhita; lived in the Gupta era.

questions.question: Which of the following Mauryan rulers did Seleucus fight against in the Seleucid-Mauryan War?
questions.solution:
• Ruler: Chandragupta Maurya
  • War: The war ended with a treaty where Seleucus gave territories and his daughter in marriage to Chandragupta.

questions.question: Ashokan Minor Rock Edicts are found in different parts of India. Which of the following is NOT a find spot of Ashokan Minor Rock Edicts in Karnataka?
questions.solution:
• Not in Karnataka: Rupnath
  • Location: Rupnath is located in Madhya Pradesh (Jabalpur district).

questions.question: Which of the following statements was quoted by Subhash Chandra Bose?
questions.option_1: First, they ignore you, then they laugh at you, then they fight you, then you win.
questions.option_2: The best way to find yourself is to lose yourself in the service of others.
questions.option_3: Live as if you were to die tomorrow. Learn as if you were to live forever.
questions.option_4: Give me blood and I will give you freedom.
questions.solution:
• Quote: Give me blood and I will give you freedom.
  • Context: This famous battle cry was used to motivate the Indian National Army (INA).

questions.question: The Vernacular Press Act of 1878 was repealed during the tenure of Viceroy ______.
questions.solution:
• Viceroy: Lord Ripon
  • Date: Repealed in 1882. Ripon is known as the 'Father of Local Self-Government' in India.

questions.question: The ancient city of Champa is believed to be the capital of ______ Mahajanapada.
questions.solution:
• Mahajanapada: Anga
  • Context: Champa was a thriving river port located in modern-day Bhagalpur, Bihar.

questions.question: Who among the following Indian freedom fighters was fondly called Gandhi Buri (Old Lady Gandhi) for her dedication towards Gandhian principles?
questions.solution:
• Person: Matangini Hazra
  • Heroism: She was shot dead by British police while leading a protest during the Quit India Movement at age 72.

questions.question: Which of the following British officers issued the infamous ‘crawling order’ whereby Indians had to crawl on all fours to pass an alley?
questions.solution:
• Officer: General Dyer
  • Event: Issued after the Jallianwala Bagh Massacre (1919) to humiliate Indians in Amritsar.

questions.question: Who among the following was the only martyr of the Quit India phase of the freedom movement who was hanged?
questions.solution:
• Martyr: Kushal Konwar
  • Context: An Assamese freedom fighter falsely accused of a train derailment during the Quit India Movement.

questions.question: Chandragupta Maurya overthrew the power of the ______ at Magadha with the aid of Kautilya and founded a glorious Mauryan empire in 322 BC.
questions.solution:
• Dynasty: Nandas
  • Fall: Dhana Nanda was the last ruler of the Nanda dynasty before being overthrown by Chandragupta.
